text:
hana: spotted repeated tiny billing bumps after yesterday's router rollout. looks like resumed streaming sessions created new ledger rows instead of reconciling. attaching short log.
raj: paste logs?
hana:
```
2026-02-11T11:02:03Z router: session=svc-9 route=us-east -> fallback
2026-02-11T11:02:03Z stream: frag=0 len=24 truncated=true toolcall=tc-3
2026-02-11T11:02:03Z billing: provisional=24 key=svc-9#0
2026-02-11T11:02:04Z stream: resume id=r-2 frag=0 len=29 suffix=true
2026-02-11T11:02:04Z billing: confirmed=29 key=svc-9#7
```
izzy: observed keys differ (frag#0 -> frag#7). router reindexed fragments on fallback.
raj: short term mitigation: billing shim should prefer reconciling if resume_id present and confirmed key is within 10s of provisional and session matches. non-invasive.
hana: agree. also add resume_origin and resume_id to billing traces so console can group these incidents.
izzy: i'll add a reconcile flag emitted when the shim suppresses a new confirmed write.
ops-bot: deploy event: router/canary v3 started at 2026-02-11T10:58 by raj
billing-bot: Note: manual adjustments still available via /billing-evidence with logs.
raj: plan: 1) implement shim reconcile rule behind flag (24h) 2) emit telemetry fields (resume_origin,resume_id,frag_reindex) 3) console: add per-route provisional vs confirmed drift sparkline (nora owns)
hana: timeline? this is spamming support for a few customers.
raj: shim patch open, will request urgent review. aiming for rollback-safe canary in 48h.
izzy: i'll add tests for resume dedupe and a fallback header propagation change in router.
billing-bot: Reminder: tag affected sessions when filing adjustments.
hana: thanks all :thumbsup:
